text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management that emphasizes flexibility and continuous improvement. Instead of working on a massive project all at once, the team breaks the work into small, manageable periods called sprints, typically lasting one to four weeks. Each sprint begins with a planning session where the team selects tasks from a prioritized list known as the product backlog. These tasks are often expressed as user stories, which describe a feature from the end-user's perspective, such as "As a customer, I want to track my order so I can see its status." The team meets daily for a quick standup to discuss progress, obstacles, and plans for the day. This iterative development process allows for regular feedback, enabling the team to adapt quickly to changes and deliver value to customers more efficiently.
